title: Why She Smiles in Public but Breaks in Private
paragraphs:
Why She Smiles in Public but Breaks in Private
The Hidden Loneliness Women Carry… and the Jesus Who Sees It All

She laughs at the table.
She responds to messages.
She shows up, performs, supports, encourages, listens…
…but somewhere deep inside, there’s a quiet ache she can’t explain.

It’s not always loud.
It doesn’t always look like tears.
Sometimes it looks like strength.
And that’s what makes it so dangerous.
Because no one checks on the “strong one.”
No one notices the woman who holds everyone together… while slowly falling apart inside.
And maybe that’s you.

Maybe you’ve been surrounded by people, yet somehow feel unseen.
Heard… but not understood.
Needed… but never truly known.
And the worst part?

You’ve prayed.
You’ve tried.
You’ve stayed faithful.
So why does your heart still feel… alone?
This isn’t new.
Long before your silent battles, Scripture recorded the same ache in the soul of a woman who thought God had forgotten her.
In Genesis, Hagar found herself abandoned, used, and discarded. She was pregnant, alone in the wilderness, and invisible to the world that had once demanded everything from her.
And yet, in that moment, something happened that changes everything.
She encountered God.
And she called Him:

“El Roi” — אֵל רֳאִי
“The God who sees me.”
“אַתָּה אֵל רֳאִי” (Atah El Ro’i) — “You are the God who sees me.” (Genesis 16:13)

Not the God who overlooks.
Not the God who forgets.
Not the God who abandons.
The God who sees.

Sees the tears you hide.
Sees the exhaustion behind your smile.
Sees the nights you cry silently so no one hears.
And here’s where it gets deeper…
The loneliness you feel isn’t just emotional.
It’s spiritual.
Because the human heart was never designed to be fully satisfied by human connection alone.
There is a space inside you that no friend, no partner, no family member can fill.
That space belongs to God.
In the Greek New Testament, Jesus speaks words that echo directly into this ache:

“Come to Me, all who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.”
“Δεῦτε πρός με πάντες οἱ κοπιῶντες καὶ πεφορτισμένοι…” (Matthew 11:28)
That word “κοπιῶντες” (kopiōntes) doesn’t just mean tired.
It means exhausted from labour… drained from carrying too much for too long.
That’s not just physical.
That’s emotional exhaustion.
That’s you holding everything together for everyone else… until there’s nothing left for yourself.
And Jesus doesn’t say, “Fix yourself first.”
He says, “Come.”

Not when you’re better.
Not when you’re stronger.
Not when you’ve figured it out.
Now.
But here’s the truth many don’t say out loud:
Sometimes the reason you feel emotionally alone… is because you’ve been pouring into everyone except the One who can actually fill you.
You’ve been seeking understanding from people… instead of intimacy with God.
You’ve been asking others to carry what only Christ can heal.
And slowly, without realising it… your soul has been starving.
David understood this kind of loneliness too.
In Psalm 142:4, he writes:
“אֵין־דֹּרֵשׁ לְנַפְשִׁי” (Ein doresh lenafshi)
That’s not just poetic.
That’s desperation.
That’s the cry of someone who feels completely unseen… even while surrounded.
But David didn’t stay there.
He turned that loneliness into surrender.
And that’s the turning point for you too.
Because loneliness can either pull you deeper into isolation…
or push you closer to God.
And the difference is what you do with it.
Maybe your loneliness isn’t a punishment.
Maybe it’s an invitation.

An invitation to stop performing.
To stop pretending.
To stop seeking validation from people who were never meant to be your source.
And to finally let God into the parts of your heart you’ve kept hidden.
Because the truth is…
Jesus doesn’t just see you.
He understands you.
On the cross, He experienced the deepest form of emotional abandonment.

“My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”
“Ἐλωΐ Ἐλωΐ λαμὰ σαβαχθανί” (Mark 15:34, Aramaic form recorded in Greek text)
That wasn’t weakness.
That was the weight of isolation, rejection, and separation.
He stepped into that darkness… so you wouldn’t have to stay there.
So your loneliness would never be the end of your story.
This is where everything shifts.
Because when you realise that Christ has already entered your loneliness…
you stop seeing it as emptiness…
and start seeing it as a place where God meets you.

A place where healing begins.
A place where identity is restored.
A place where love becomes real… not just something you give, but something you receive.
So if you’ve been feeling emotionally alone…
this is not your ending.
This is your encounter.
And maybe… right now… this moment…
is God reminding you:
“I see you. I’ve always seen you.”
Be honest.
This hit somewhere deeper than you expected, didn’t it?
Don’t keep this to yourself.
And if you want to go deeper… if you’re serious about growing in Christ, healing fully, and walking in truth…
stay close.
And for those who are ready to take their faith seriously…
You don’t support this just for content.
You support this to advance the Kingdom.
Because the truth is…
someone else’s healing might be on the other side of your obedience to share this.
And long after the noise fades… this will still echo in your spirit:
God saw you… even when you thought no one did.
